mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows two distinct AuditEntry atoms for the same application to share identical (prevStat, newStat) values, modelling an in-place mutation or replay of an existing audit row. The injection forces exactly such a duplicate pair to exist, which both AppendOnly and FR_018_AuditImmutable must catch.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj ae1, ae2 : AuditEntry | ae1.forApp = ae2.forApp and ae1.prevStat = ae2.prevStat and ae1.newStat = ae2.newStat }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact permits an AuditEntry where the officer who performed the transition is also the applicant of that application. The injection forces a state where a non-initial audit entry exists whose actorUser equals the application's own applicant and actorRole is ROfficer, directly violating FR-013.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NoSelfApprovalViolation { some ae : AuditEntry | some ae.prevStat and ae.actorRole = ROfficer and ae.actorUser = ae.forApp.applicant }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows arbitrary cells in PermMatrix.Allowed, including RAuditor → OpPost and RAuditor → OpPatch. The injection adds the auditor-to-post cell, which directly violates both LeastPrivilege (a denied cell is now allowed) and PermissionCompleteness (the matrix no longer matches the spec).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_PermissionMatrixViolation { RAuditor -> OpPost in PermMatrix.Allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact permits an application at status UnderReview to exist with only one audit entry (the initial submission entry), meaning the Pending→UnderReview transition has no corresponding audit record. The injection forces exactly this situation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCountViolation { some app : LoanApplication | app.status = UnderReview and (one ae : AuditEntry | ae.forApp = app) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows a successful OpPatch by a caller who is not the application's assigned officer, violating the core access-control invariant that only the assigned officer may transition status. The injection forces a successful PATCH by a user who is demonstrably not the assigned officer.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnershipBasedAccessViolation { some op : Operation | op.kind = OpPatch and op.outcome = OpSuccess and some op.targetApp and op.callerUser != op.targetApp.assignedOfficer }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows a denied GET operation to carry a non-null targetApp reference, meaning the response distinguishes 'exists but caller cannot access' from 'does not exist' — breaking the byte-equivalence guarantee. The injection forces a denied GET to reference an existing application.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_InformationLeakageViolation { some op : Operation | op.kind = OpGet and op.outcome = OpDenied and some op.targetApp }
